parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the approximate C1–C2–C3 angle and C2–C3–C4 angle, explaining the difference.

steps.text: C1 and C2: sp; C3 and C4: sp².
Three π bonds in total: two in the triple bond and one in the double bond.
Approximately 180° at C2 and 120° at C3.
C2 has two electron domains; C3 has three. Multiple bonds count as one domain for VSEPR.

title: Inferring charge from a crystal
stem: An ionic compound contains metal ions $\mathrm{M^{3+}}$ and oxide ions. It has a high melting point and is brittle.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Deduce its simplest formula and explain the high melting point.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the lattice model to explain brittleness.

steps.text: M₂O₃, because 2(+3)+3(−2)=0.
Strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions throughout the lattice require substantial energy to overcome.
A displacement can bring like-charged ions into adjacent positions.
Repulsion between them causes the lattice to split rather than allowing sustained sliding.
